document_title: Alaska's Second Wire Has a Passenger List
post_copy:
Alaska's planned second power line would end at Healy, south of Clear and Eielson, where the Air Force offered land for AI data centers.

It would run about 223 miles from Beluga through West Susitna and Willow.

Clear, Eielson and JBER hold the 12 parcels offered this spring. Lisa Murkowski told the American Homefront Project she isn't a proponent of data centers there because of "an insecure energy base at this time."

The Energy Department intends up to $150 million, citing the military and mining.

The wire is still in planning. The land had no award by late September. No record behind the wire says data center.

Today's intertie, the new wire's stops and money, three bases and Murkowski's sentence, then five records, two saying data center.

Why is the record for a Defense Production Act line silent on data centers offered for Railbelt bases?

#Railbelt #BelugaHealy #AlaskaGrid

slides.headline: Alaska's second wire has a passenger list.
The money names the military, and mining.
slides.body: Energy Secretary Chris Wright tied the project to "the major U.S. military expansion currently underway in Alaska" and to mining. DOE says the line adds a pathway to "major military installations." The release never says data center.
labels: GOLD · ALASKA INTERTIE BLUE · MILITARY BASES

slides.headline: One line joins the two halves today.
slides.body: AEA's Alaska Intertie runs 170 miles from Willow to Healy. The state built it in the mid-1980s.
labels: PROFILE ALONG THE LINE · VERTICAL SCALE EXAGGERATED

slides.headline: The record names its stops and its price. Not its route.
slides.body: The Alaska delegation lists the Beluga substation, West Susitna, Willow and Healy. AEA's Curtis Thayer told the Alaska Beacon the federal money will likely go to engineering, planning and permitting.
labels: LATE AUGUST · AEA LISTS IT "UNDER CONSIDERATION" OCTOBER 5TH · DOE NAMES IT
NAMED STOPS · IN ORDER, NOT TO DISTANCE
UP TO $150 MILLION · DEFENSE PRODUCTION ACT

slides.kicker: THIS SPRING · DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
slides.headline: On Railbelt bases, land offered for AI data centers.
slides.body: Proposals were due June 29th. None had been awarded as of late September, per the American Homefront Project. Most of Alaska's bases use power that flows through the intertie, the Alaska Beacon reports.
labels: 12 PARCELS · ABOUT 4,700 ACRES · ACROSS ALL THREE

slides.headline: One corridor. No second path between the halves.
labels: ILLUSTRATION, NOT A SURVEYED STRUCTURE · NOON

slides.kicker: MURKOWSKI · TO THE AMERICAN HOMEFRONT PROJECT
slides.headline: "I am not a proponent of data centers down at JBER or at our interior installations because we are not able to support them because of an insecure energy base at this time."
Five records. Two say "data center." The one with the money doesn't.
slides.body: Reading them side by side is this deck's work, not DOE's.
